Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a workout into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme workout and deliver a live timeline: Erg Session — four rowers, two machines for 4 rowers, 2 ergs, 3 pieces
Resource limits: two ergs, four rowers, one coach, one rower on the coached drill at a time.
No finishing time was given; finish as early as the work allows.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Erg Session — four rowers, two machines

Two ergs in the bay and four of us, so we row in pairs and the pair that is off the machines is the pair that is resting. A and B are the first pair, C and D the second. Nobody sits on a machine they are not rowing.

Warm-up
A and B warm up first: 10 minutes, rate 18, light pressure, half slide to full slide.
C and D come in ten minutes later and take the machines for their own 10 minute warm-up.

The pieces
Three pieces, four minutes each, rate 26 to 28, target split on the monitor.
A and B take the first piece as soon as C and D are off the machines.
C and D take the first piece straight off the back of A and B's first piece.
A and B start their second piece four minutes after their first one ends.
C and D take the second piece as soon as A and B are off.
A and B start their third piece four minutes after their second one ends.
C and D take the third piece as soon as A and B are off.

Technique drill
Three minutes each, one at a time, coach on the machine with you: pause at the finish, pause at half slide, then build. A goes first once C and D are off the last piece, then B, then C, then D.

Cooldown
Ten minutes on the floor together once the last drill is done: legs up the wall, hips, lats, then a cup of tea.

Coach
Brief the crew on the boards before anyone gets on: 5 minutes.
Call splits from the first piece: 20 minutes on the clock, watch the catch not the monitor.
Run the drills: 12 minutes, one rower at a time, straight through.
Debrief after the cooldown: 10 minutes, what the splits said and what Saturday looks like.

Note
The rests are not steps for the first pair: they are the gap between one piece ending and the next one starting, because the machines are handed over in that gap and the second pair is using them. The second pair's rests are the first pair's pieces. That is the whole design of the session.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

End your reply with the same read-back as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json

  "summary": "one paragraph: what is being made, for how many, by when, under what constraints",
```

This is a Rhylthyme workout timeline for one coach and four rowers using only two erg machines. The crew splits into two pairs, A/B and C/D, so the session is fundamentally a machine handoff exercise: while one pair rows a four-minute piece, the other pair is off the machines in the gap before its next piece, and the three pieces per pair alternate this way. The coach has separate duties that must be held or started at specific moments: a five-minute briefing before anyone gets on, split-calling for twenty minutes from the first piece, twelve minutes of coached drills one rower at a time after the last piece, and a ten-minute debrief after the ten-minute floor cooldown. There is no requested deadline, so the program should finish as early as the mandatory sequence, the two-machine limit, the one-at-a-time drill limit, and the need for the four rowers to do the cooldown together allow. The source does not appear truncated; the exact target split on the monitor is unspecified, but it does not change the timing.

completion.text:
A Rhylthyme track is one sequential line of work; its steps cannot overlap, while anything that happens at the same time belongs in a separate track. A step has exactly one duration kind: `fixed` with `seconds`, `variable` with `minSeconds`, `maxSeconds`, and `defaultSeconds`, or `indefinite` until the person ends it. A startTrigger anchors that step to `programStart`, `programStartOffset`, another step via `afterStep`, a buffered after-step trigger, a manual tap, an abort, or a compound condition. `stepId`s are unique across the whole program, not just within one track. Every `task` occupied by a step needs a matching `resourceConstraints` entry, and that entry’s `maxConcurrent` is the shared-resource limiter, such as one oven, one coach, or two ergs. Repeated work should use `replicates` on one step rather than copied steps or tracks, chaining per-instance work with `instances: "each"`, barrier steps with `instances: "all"`, and using `maxInFlight` when a holding area only fits `k` instances at once.

Resource constraints I expect for this workout:

- `erg` — `maxConcurrent: 2` — two rowing machines; four rowers use them in pairs, but only two rower-machine steps can overlap at once.
- `coach` — `maxConcurrent: 1` — one coach; one coach handles briefing, split calling, drills, and debrief.
- `coached_drill` — `maxConcurrent: 1` — one rower at a time on the coached drill; this is the explicit drill slot, with one rower plus the coach working at that moment.
- `floor` — `maxConcurrent: 5` — cooldown floor work; four rowers are together on the floor, and the coach may also be present, so five people are the maximum occupied there.
- `actors` — five people total: four rowers and one coach. Rests between pieces should not be declared as machine-rest resources; they are timing gaps created by handoffs.

```json
{
  "acknowledgement": "tracks are sequential lines of work; one duration kind per step; triggers link steps or the clock; stepIds are global; every task needs a resourceConstraint; repeated work uses replicates with instances each/all and maxInFlight only for holding-area limits",
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "erg", "maxConcurrent": 2 },
    { "task": "coach", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "coached_drill", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "floor", "maxConcurrent": 5 }
  ],
  "actors": 5
}
```
